identity.public_title: Danse - a room that never repeats

copy.eyebrow: A living photographic work begun in 2017
copy.logline: A room reconstructed from one afternoon of photographs becomes a seeded, unbounded choreography that can be revisited but never rewound.
copy.concept: In June 2017, a locked camera watched a dancer move through a South Florida apartment. The surviving photographs share one viewpoint and one architecture. Danse treats those records as spatial material: fragments from different instants can occupy depth while a single projector model keeps the room continuous. The work is not one fixed film. Each visit enters a deterministic river whose exact state can be cited by seed and time.
copy.installation_concept: The installation returns photographic fragments to physical space. Projected planes or scrim surfaces carry views from the same camera position, allowing a flat composite to open into a room as viewpoint, depth, and visitor input diverge. Venue geometry, projection, sound, recovery, and safety remain proposals until issue 14 supplies validated evidence.
copy.technical_summary: The visual engine is a pure function of a 32-bit seed and absolute river time. It can seek directly to any state without replaying earlier frames. Entropy and wall-clock access remain isolated in the visitor-arrival boundary; release claims about final score, room synchronization, recovery, and capture quality remain gated by their exact receipts.

accessibility.canvas_description: A generative WebGL composition draws registered fragments from 162 photographs made in one apartment session. The same seed and time reproduce the same arrangement.
accessibility.motion_note: The default artwork contains continuous drift, changes in depth, and camera divergence. Some passages may include faster reseeding transitions.
accessibility.audio_note: Final score, sound design, spatial behavior, loudness, and captionable sound events remain pending; no release claim is made from the provisional soundtrack text.

press.synopsis_short: In 2017 a dancer moved through a Florida apartment while the camera stood still. One hundred sixty-two photographs now feed a generative room that can reproduce any cited instant without repeating the river around it.
press.synopsis_long: On 20 June 2017, a locked camera recorded a dancer moving through a one-bedroom apartment in South Florida. Because every exposure shares one viewpoint, fragments from different instants can align to the same architecture. A hand-cut composite made that summer lay dormant for nine years. Danse returns to it as a living system: a pure seeded engine reconstructs the flat work, opens its fragments into depth, and lets each visitor enter a river with a durable identity. The final score-driven film, spatial sound, and physical installation remain separate evidence-gated forms of that same engine.
press.artist_bio: Anthony J. Padavano is a photographer and programmer working between South Florida and New York. His work treats a photograph as a record of where a camera stood and software as part of the photographic object. Final identity and biography wording require the artist's approval before publication.
press.artist_statement: The original collage was cut by feeling. The generative work asks what those fragments become when they are treated as views through one camera instead of flat pieces of paper. Nothing in the image needs to be invented: each fragment comes from the same afternoon and remains accountable to its source. The release statement will be artist-approved only after the score-driven cut, room behavior, and rights register are complete.
